Scenario Agent Skills



Agent Skills that teach AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and 70+ others) how to create production-ready content with [Scenario](https://scenario.com) through the [Scenario MCP server](https://mcp.scenario.com): images, video, audio, textures, skyboxes, 3D assets, and custom-trained models, for games, entertainment, and any creative vertical. The expert tools at the bottom of the list work differently: teams of skills that drive DCC (digital content creation) software and game engines installed on your machine (ZBrush, Blender, Maya, Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot, Roblox Studio), distilled from expert tutorials, conference talks, and official documentation. They need the application, not the Scenario MCP server, and each family folder's README records how it was built and how far it was verified. Skills follow the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format. ## Install **Everything for Scenario.** Every Scenario skill, without the expert tools: the default for working through the Scenario MCP. ```bash # Every Scenario skill, without the expert tools npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill scenario scenario-inspiration scenario-image scenario-multi-reference scenario-product-shots scenario-brand-kit scenario-image-editing scenario-text-overlay scenario-storyboards scenario-game-assets scenario-sprite-animation scenario-side-view-game-kit scenario-blender-2d-animation scenario-textures scenario-skyboxes scenario-3d scenario-video-to-motion scenario-blender scenario-patina-retexture scenario-orbit-views scenario-walkable-room scenario-video scenario-video-editing scenario-ad-variants scenario-thumbnails ``` **By role or goal.** [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) groups the skills by job, from 2D artist to producer, and by outcome, from game art to ChatGPT pets, with one command each. **Expert tools.** A family installs as one set, since its specialists import the lead skill's scripts: select its "Expert tools" group in the installer menu, or run the command in its family README ([ZBrush](skills/dcc/zbrush/README.md), [Blender](skills/dcc/blender/README.md), [Maya](skills/dcc/maya/README.md), [Unreal Engine](skills/game-engines/unreal/README.md), [Unity](skills/game-engines/unity/README.md), [Godot](skills/game-engines/godot/README.md), [Roblox Studio](skills/game-engines/roblox/README.md)). **Pick, or install one skill.** ```bash # Pick from the installer menu, grouped by topic (it opens with nothing preselected: select before pressing enter) npx skills add scenario-labs/skills # A single skill npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill scenario ``` **Pin a reviewed release.** The commands above fetch the latest copy of each skill from `main`. To install a reviewed state instead, pin both the installer and the commit, taken from a release's tag. Run it again with a newer commit to move. ```bash npx skills@1.7.4 add scenario-labs/skills# --skill ``` The menu's topic groups cannot be selected from the command line: the CLI matches `--skill` against exact skill names only, and a group flag is an open request upstream ([vercel-labs/skills#992](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/992)). From a script or CI, run the default command above or a role command from INSTALL.md with `-y`, which skips every prompt. The Scenario skills need the Scenario MCP server connected: ```bash claude mcp add --transport http scenario https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp ``` Or add `https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp` to any MCP client and sign in with a Scenario account (OAuth), or use an [API key](https://app.scenario.com/settings/api). Full setup lives in the `scenario` skill. ## Staying up to date Releases are how changes become visible: every feature, fix, and documentation change merged to `main` lands in the next release, staged by release-please as an open release PR. An entry scoped to a single skill carries that skill's name; changes spanning several skills appear under broader scopes such as `skills`. - To pull the changes, run `npx skills update` where you Scenario Agent Skills



Agent Skills that teach AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and 70+ others) how to create production-ready content with Scenario through the Scenario MCP server: images, video, audio, textures, skyboxes, 3D assets, and custom-trained models, for games, entertainment, and any creative vertical.

The expert tools at the bottom of the list work differently: teams of skills that drive DCC (digital content creation) software and game engines installed on your machine (ZBrush, Blender, Maya, Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot, Roblox Studio), distilled from expert tutorials, conference talks, and official documentation. They need the application, not the Scenario MCP server, and each family folder's README records how it was built and how far it was verified.

Skills follow the Agent Skills format.

Install

Everything for Scenario. Every Scenario skill, without the expert tools: the default for working through the Scenario MCP.

# Every Scenario skill, without the expert tools
npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill scenario scenario-inspiration scenario-image scenario-multi-reference scenario-product-shots scenario-brand-kit scenario-image-editing scenario-text-overlay scenario-storyboards scenario-game-assets scenario-sprite-animation scenario-side-view-game-kit scenario-blender-2d-animation scenario-textures scenario-skyboxes scenario-3d scenario-video-to-motion scenario-blender scenario-patina-retexture scenario-orbit-views scenario-walkable-room scenario-video scenario-video-editing scenario-video-color-grade scenario-seedance-music-video scenario-kinetic-music-video scenario-chatgpt-pet-create scenario-chatgpt-pet-update scenario-seedance-storyboard scenario-seedance-drafts scenario-video-ads scenario-ugc scenario-fan-cam scenario-reel-recast scenario-audio scenario-video-assembly scenario-motion-loops scenario-caption-studio scenario-consistency scenario-identity-library scenario-model-training scenario-asset-analysis scenario-quality-gate scenario-refine-loop scenario-model-comparison scenario-formats scenario-workflows scenario-workflow-authoring scenario-moderation scenario-report scenario-team-admin scenario-admin-analytics scenario-gpt-image scenario-mai-image scenario-seedream scenario-gemini-image scenario-reve scenario-ideogram scenario-grok-imagine-image scenario-luma-image scenario-minimax-video scenario-gemini-omni scenario-grok-imagine-video scenario-veo scenario-seedance scenario-kling scenario-vidu scenario-wan scenario-runway scenario-luma-video scenario-minimax-music scenario-elevenlabs scenario-ace-step scenario-sonilo scenario-meshy scenario-rodin scenario-sparc3d scenario-3d-worlds scenario-ad-variants scenario-thumbnails

By role or goal. INSTALL.md groups the skills by job, from 2D artist to producer, and by outcome, from game art to ChatGPT pets, with one command each.

Expert tools. A family installs as one set, since its specialists import the lead skill's scripts: select its "Expert tools" group in the installer menu, or run the command in its family README (ZBrush, Blender, Maya, Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot, Roblox Studio).

Pick, or install one skill.

# Pick from the installer menu, grouped by topic (it opens with nothing preselected: select before pressing enter)
npx skills add scenario-labs/skills

# A single skill
npx skills add scenario-labs/skills --skill scenario

Pin a reviewed release. The commands above fetch the latest copy of each skill from main. To install a reviewed state instead, pin both the installer and the commit, taken from a release's tag. Run it again with a newer commit to move.

npx skills@1.7.4 add scenario-labs/skills#<commit> --skill <name>

The menu's topic groups cannot be selected from the command line: the CLI matches --skill against exact skill names only, and a group flag is an open request upstream (vercel-labs/skills#992). From a script or CI, run the default command above or a role command from INSTALL.md with -y, which skips every prompt.

The Scenario skills need the Scenario MCP server connected:

claude mcp add --transport http scenario https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp

Or add https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp to any MCP client and sign in with a Scenario account (OAuth), or use an API key. Full setup lives in the scenario skill.

Staying up to date

Releases are how changes become visible: every feature, fix, and documentation change merged to main lands in the next release, staged by release-please as an open release PR. Merging that PR tags a version, updates CHANGELOG.md in this repository, publishes a GitHub release, and posts the notes to the Scenario changelog.

  • To learn that a skill changed, watch this repository's releases (Watch, then Custom, then Releases on GitHub) or check any of the changelog pages above. An entry scoped to a single skill carries that skill's name; changes spanning several skills appear under broader scopes such as skills.
  • To pull the changes, run npx skills update where you installed, or re-run your original npx skills add command.
  • To stay on a reviewed state, pin the install (see Install).

Skills

Getting started

Connect the Scenario MCP server and learn the core generation loop every other skill builds on.

Skill Use it for
scenario Connecting to the Scenario MCP and the core generation loop: discover, schema, run, wait, display, download

Finding a direction

Turn a blank brief into references, options someone can choose between, and a moodboard the next batch runs from.

Skill Use it for
scenario-inspiration Finding a direction before generating: serendipity, reference hunting, A/B/C/D concept options, moodboard collections

Images

Generate and edit images: model choice, sizing, references, masked edits, post-processing tools, and letter-perfect text overlay cards.

Skill Use it for
scenario-image Text-to-image and image editing: model choice, sizing fields, prompt limits, reference images, masked inpainting
scenario-multi-reference One image composed from several references, each with one job (subject, place, pose, style, palette), leaks checked
scenario-product-shots Product photography from a real photo: packshots, lifestyle scenes, relighting, label-fidelity gates
scenario-brand-kit Visual identities: SVG logos and wordmarks, palette and type specs, gated variants and applications, the filed kit
scenario-image-editing Tool-model image edits: 3D LUT grades, effects, expand and reframe, resize, slicing, layers, background removal
scenario-text-overlay Letter-perfect text overlays: templated transparent PNG cards (taglines, CTAs, legal supers, rich cards) to composite
scenario-storyboards Comic pages, storybooks, and pre-viz storyboards: script first, one run per panel, a locked cast, lettering in post
scenario-thumbnails Finished video covers with character fidelity, exact copy and small-preview readability

Game art and 3D

Sprites, icons, tilesets, textures, skyboxes, 3D models, and walkable spaces for games, the web, and interactive scenes.

Skill Use it for
scenario-game-assets Sprites, icons, props, tilesets, pixel art, concept art, transparent backgrounds, style-consistent batches
scenario-sprite-animation Walk cycles, idle loops, VFX sprites, and animation sheets from one prompt: GIF vs sprite sheet output, frame slicing, pixel cleanup
scenario-side-view-game-kit Side-scroller and platformer art: side-view pixel sprite strips for a hero and enemies (run, walk, attack, hurt, poses), parallax layers, seamless wall texture, platform strip, props
scenario-blender-2d-animation A side-scroller shot animated in Blender from Scenario pictures: a concept frame that locks the look, parallax layers, props and a hero run cycle on its reference, flat image cards with an orthographic camera, keyed jumps and rigid-body props, and a whole new look by swapping the pictures
scenario-textures Seamless and tileable textures, PBR materials, tiling-safe upscaling, engine-ready sizing
scenario-skyboxes 360 equirectangular panoramas and skyboxes, seam-safe upscaling, engine export
scenario-3d Text or image to 3D meshes, multi-view reconstruction, retexture and remesh, inline 3D preview, GLB/FBX download
scenario-video-to-motion Motion capture from a reference or generated video: an uploaded character auto-rigged and animated, or motion alone on a Mixamo or MetaHuman skeleton, with in-place, looping, and engine-ready exports
scenario-blender Drive an open Blender scene through the Scenario for Blender extension's local MCP server: read the scene, quote and run generations, capture viewport references, place results, plan camera paths
scenario-patina-retexture PATINA PBR retexture of a finished mesh: material families, one map set per family, Blender apply with geometry untouched, matched before/after comparison film
scenario-orbit-views New camera angles of one picture through a 3D intermediary: clay layouts in a grounded panorama, repaint per camera, matched transparent set
scenario-walkable-room A room from one interior photo to walk into: clean plate, splat world, PBR props with impact sounds, splat-based calibration, physics viewer with grab and throw

Video and audio

Video generation, editing, and color grading, seamless motion loops, music, sound effects, voice, and speech.

Skill Use it for
scenario-video Text-to-video and image-to-video, motion prompting, lipsync, video editing, upscaling, cut/split/concat utilities
scenario-video-editing Tool-model footage edits: LUT grades and effects, trim, split, resize, reverse, frames, masks, layers
scenario-video-color-grade Code-written grades on existing footage: looks, relight, log to Rec.709, reference match, one kept color with masks, .cube LUTs, a showreel
scenario-seedance-music-video Turning a song into a music video: beat-aligned shots, lyric transcription, shot sound under the master, assembly
scenario-seedance-storyboard Movement that holds across cuts: timecoded shot scripts, character sheets and boards, pose-chained shots that play as one performance
scenario-seedance-drafts Cheap 480p Seedance takes reviewed and ranked, only the picks finalized to 1080p, with the draft-versus-final cost math
scenario-video-ads Producing a video ad from a product shot: brief, storyboard, cinematic grammar, fidelity gates, budget, delivery
scenario-ad-variants Ordered independent campaign edits from existing footage, preserving original gameplay and audio
scenario-audio Music, sound effects, voice and speech generation, video scoring, audio utilities
scenario-video-assembly Assembling clips into a finished video: timeline composition, concat with transitions, overlays, music, captions
scenario-motion-loops Seamless brand-color motion loops in code (backgrounds, bumpers, shape animations) rendered to MP4, with a Scenario cut-out over them
scenario-caption-studio Captioning a finished video per destination: styled burn-in or SRT, transcription hints, translation, per-platform placement

Socials

Made for social feeds and chat apps: UGC-style creator videos, fan-cam reactions from a photo, trend reels recast with your own character, kinetic-typography lyric videos, and animated ChatGPT and Codex pets, new or updated.

Skill Use it for
scenario-ugc UGC-style creator video: talking-head and avatar ads, demos, faceless voiceover, spoken-register scripts, claim safety
scenario-fan-cam Personalized fan-cam clips: identity edit into a broadcast still, reaction beats to video, graphics composited in post
scenario-reel-recast A trending reel performed again by your character: same moves, camera and song, outfit swaps, a redecorated room
scenario-kinetic-music-video Kinetic-typography music video, landscape or 9:16: style frames and footage from Scenario, a JavaScript engine for lyric type on sung onsets, mattes, per-section agents
scenario-chatgpt-pet-create ChatGPT or Codex pet from an idea or photos: a v2 sprite sheet with sixteen look directions, a v1 copy for web upload, pixel-perfect mode, GIFs, a Codex package
scenario-chatgpt-pet-update Change an existing pet sheet: fix or redo a row, add look directions to a v1 sheet, a new outfit or color, a rename, a check and GIF preview

Consistency and custom models

Hold one character, product, or style across a whole set, and train custom models on your own art.

Skill Use it for
scenario-consistency Holding one character, product, or style across a set: baseline-plus-delta prompts, reference images, control maps
scenario-identity-library Creating named characters and props as reusable identities: interview to brief, gated collections, Grid Maker sheets, reuse
scenario-model-training Training custom models for style, character, or product consistency, and generating with them

Reviewing and organizing output

Read finished assets back: caption them, extract a style or a control map, check a batch against a brief or the Quality Gate, compare candidate models on one brief, and file the keepers.

Skill Use it for
scenario-asset-analysis Reading assets back: captions, style descriptions, batch review against a brief, control maps, collections, tags
scenario-quality-gate Pass/warn/fail image verdicts from the Quality Gate: free stored reads, dry-run pricing, feeding suggestions back into the next run
scenario-refine-loop Iterating until output matches the brief: rubric first, batched critique verdicts, cheapest targeted fix, round caps

Example prompts

Once the skills are installed and the MCP server is connected, ask your agent things like:

  • "Generate four style-matched potion icons with transparent backgrounds for my RPG inventory"
  • "Make a seamless brick texture, then upscale it to 2048 without breaking the tiling"
  • "Turn this concept sketch into a 3D prop and let me preview it before I export the GLB"

What is an Agent Skill?

A skill is a SKILL.md file with procedural knowledge an agent loads on demand, defined by the open Agent Skills specification. The skills CLI installs these files into 70+ agents, and the ecosystem directory lives at skills.sh.

Contributing

See CONTRIBUTING.md for the contribution workflow, and AGENTS.md for the authoring contract, the public-content policy, validation, and the application-testing bar. One-time setup after cloning: install the prerequisites, uv included, then run pnpm install (installs commitlint, cspell, prettier, and the husky git hooks). pnpm run validate runs the same content checks CI runs; commit messages and the PR title are linted separately with commitlint. PRs welcome; PR titles follow Conventional Commits since they become the squash commit header on main.

Every script shipped with a skill has a test suite in tests/<name>/; pnpm test runs them all (CI does too). Suites need Python 3.11+, plus ffmpeg on PATH where a suite uses it. With uv installed, pnpm test gives each suite the dependencies in its tests/<name>/requirements.txt; without uv, install them into python3 first. Python suites use stdlib unittest, TypeScript suites use vitest.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A framework providing expert tools and skills for Scenario MCP servers.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Skills provides a standardized format for defining agent capabilities for Scenario. It allows users to install various skills for 2D, 3D, and video generation. The repository includes expert tools for integrating with digital content creation software. It connects to the Scenario MCP server to execute these capabilities. This helps users quickly assemble complex creative workflows.
keyFeatures: Skill definition: provides a standardized Agent Skills format for defining capabilities.
Modular installation: allows installing specific groups of skills via a command-line interface.
Expert tools: includes integrations for popular DCC software like Blender and Unreal Engine.
MCP server integration: connects to the Scenario MCP server for executing generation loops.
Creative workflows: supports complex tasks from text-to-image to 3D model generation.
